text:
maria_dev: Heads-up — opened a PR to consolidate provider blocks across our shared modules and to centralize provider pinning. Ran `terraform init` locally and CI updated `.terraform.lock.hcl`. Now the platform-prod repo CI is failing with a provider checksum/version mismatch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3481

leo_infra: link looks good, will take a look. Can you paste the `required_providers` snippet from the root?

maria_dev: sure — in modules/common/providers.tf I changed to a single root provider block and pinned aws to `~> 5.0` and removed duplicate aliases. snippet:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
}
```
CI updated the lockfile after `terraform init` which is probably what tripped the downstream job.

samir: quick note — `.terraform.lock.hcl` includes provider checksums that are specific to platform/arch and provider package digests. If infra CI ran on macOS arm64 but platform-prod runs linux_amd64, you'll see checksum mismatches unless lockfile contains both checksums.

ashley: also, I modified how KMS keys are wired in the refactor — moved the key id into a module output and changed the Vault path consumers use. Did any consumers get updated to read the new output name? That could also cause downstream failures but sounds orthogonal to the provider checksum issue.

maria_dev: good catch — I updated the consumer in the app module for the vault path, but platform-prod uses a pinned module ref (v2.4.1) and hasn't picked up my module changes. The failing CI log shows: `terraform provider registry plugin checksum mismatch` followed by `expected` vs `actual` checksums.

leo_infra: two immediate paths: 1) regress the lockfile change in this PR (keep the provider refactor but revert the `.terraform.lock.hcl` update) so downstream CI stays stable, then regenerate lockfile in a controlled job that matches target CI platform; or 2) regenerate the lockfile including all CI/platform targets using `terraform providers lock -platform` for each arch.

samir: exact command that helps: `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_arm64 -platform=linux_arm64` which will record checksums for those platforms. Terraform will then accept those checksums when running on any of them. After that run `terraform init` and commit the updated `.terraform.lock.hcl`.

ashley: another practical short-term mitigation is to unstage the lockfile change from this PR and push the provider consolidation only. Then trigger a separate infra job (running on linux_amd64) to run the lock commands and commit the lockfile once we confirm checksums.

maria_dev: OK I'll do option to revert the lockfile change in this branch and leave the provider code changes. Will open a follow-up that runs lock generation in infra CI targeting linux_amd64.

leo_infra: also add a note in the PR description about the arch/multi-platform lockfile issue so downstream teams aren't surprised.

ashley: +1. For the KMS/vault wiring: I'll open a tiny PR to bump the module ref in platform-prod to pick up the output name change once we merge.

ops-bot: CI: platform-prod build failure 1764510189 — reason: provider checksum mismatch. See job: https://ci.internal.redwood/teams/platform-prod/builds/9821

maria_dev: thanks all — reverting lockfile now and will ping when the regen-run has landed. Would anyone like to pair on the lock regen so we can test on both linux_amd64 and darwin_arm64?

samir: I can join for the regen in ~30m. Also recommend we add a short checklist to infra README about regenerating `.terraform.lock.hcl` across supported platforms.

leo_infra: sounds good. I'll add checklist entry after this lands.
